title: The comment thread card draws @mentions in the brand colour, like the chat column's Comments list
steps: S1: From vendor/tracy/dsh-better-sidebar run: npx vitest run tests/thread-mention-parts.spec.ts tests/comment-people-layer.spec.tsx -t "mention"
S2: Read the exit code and the passed / failed counts, and the tests named below.
S3: Read src/client/sidebar.module.css and find the .threadMention rule.
expect: 'cuts every mention out of the words, in order', 'a mention after text, and a trailing dot left out' and 'never an e-mail address, and plain words stay one part' pass: `mentionParts('@octopal @anhvp.ecom cái này')` returns the two mentions as their own parts, and `a@b.co` is never a mention.

'each mention in its own span with the mention class; an e-mail address stays plain' passes: a thread with '@octopal @anhvp.ecom cái này' and a reply 'kìa @anhvp.ecom, mail a@b.co' renders exactly three `[data-mention]` spans with the `threadMention` class, and the message text reads unchanged.
S3: .threadMention paints `color` from `--primary` mixed with `--dsw-alias-label-primary`, weight 500.
evidence: On cowork.tracy.site 05/10/2026: the Comments list showed '@octopal @anhvp.ecom' in terracotta while the thread card printed them as plain text. The DOM test was red on the base (`expected [] to deeply equal [...]`).
fence: Mechanism only, no stand: the real CommentOverlay renders under vitest with a fixture comment mode. Not covered: painting in a real browser, the dark/light theme values, the live thread popover on a site.
